content: 1. The Bangkok Tenofovir Study Group conducted a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 trial to evaluate the efficacy of antiretroviral prophylaxis for preventing HIV infection among injecting drug users in Bangkok, Thailand. The findings were published in the Lancet, volume 381, issue 9883, pages 2083-2090, in 2013. 2. Brozek and Schunemann, in 2011, provided guidelines for rating the quality of evidence, specifically addressing study limitations and the risk of bias. This work was published in the Journal of Clinical Epidemiology, volume 64, pages 407-415. 3. The Cochrane Handbook for Systematic Reviews of Interventions, authored by Green and others in 2011, serves as a comprehensive guide for conducting systematic reviews. It was accessed online on June 10, 2011. 4. Clarke, Jaffe, and Cates conducted a phase 2, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial in 2007 to assess the use of tenofovir disoproxil fumarate for HIV prevention in women. The results were published in PLoS Clinical Trials, volume 2, issue 5, article e27. 5. The Bangkok Tenofovir Study Group also investigated HIV-associated risk behaviors among injecting drug users participating in an HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis trial in Bangkok, Thailand. This research was presented as a poster (MOLBPE27) at the IAS 2013 conference. 6. UNAIDS published the Global Report: UNAIDS Report on the Global AIDS Epidemic 2013, which provides a comprehensive overview of the global HIV/AIDS situation. This report was accessed on March 2, 2014. 7. The World Health Organization (WHO) conducted a systematic review in 2014 to inform its consolidated guidelines on HIV prevention, diagnosis, treatment, and care for key populations, including pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) for people who inject drugs (PWID). 8. Eisingerich, Wheelock, Gomez, Garnett, Dybul, and Piot conducted a multinational study in 2012 to assess attitudes and acceptance of oral and parenteral HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis among potential user groups. This study provided valuable insights into the preferences and perceptions of these populations.
